title: 1. Go shopping
text: PLAN: You must plan the menus in advance to know what to buy. Order is essential in food. Planning will help us make a varied and healthier diet. SHOPPING LIST: Always make a shopping list before leaving home. Buy seasonal foods. This avoids unnecessary purchases, saves money, does not throw away food and does not eat too much SHOPPING AFTER HAVING EATEN: Do not go shopping hungry. Always go after eating. If you go hungry you will buy caloric foods that you do NOT need or that you should not eat. DON'T BUY MORE: Buy only what you need for each day. If you buy too much you will overeat. It helps to avoid having foods at home that encourage us to snack. DO NOT STORE: Do not store food at home, especially easy-to-eat foods (chocolates, bagged fried foods, nuts, industrial pastries, etc.) COOK EVERYTHING AT ONCE, and freeze in small portions what is not going to be consumed. It is a way to maintain food safety and have order in meals. AVOID TEMPTATIONS: Avoid going through the aisles of snacks and pastries, this way you will avoid temptations of foods that usually provide a lot of calories and do not benefit us. GO WITH THE RIGHT MONEY, This way you will buy only what is on the list and avoid buying in excess and save money READ THE FOOD LABELS: Read the food labeling, this way you will know the composition of the food and you will be able to choose better, they will also inform us of the expiration date and the conservation standards for these DO NOT USE LARGE CARTS. In large stores, do your shopping with a basket instead of a cart, so we will only take the essentials

title: 2. Healthy cooking
text: TRADITIONAL FOOD. Traditional food usually provides many nutrients necessary for a normal diet. Nowadays there are prepared or pre-cooked foods that help us, such as already cooked pasta or legumes. LITTLE FAT. Fat provides many calories. You have to learn to cook without adding a lot of fat to stews. Measure the oil by tablespoons. Avoid frying. FRUIT AND VEGETABLES. Fruit and vegetables provide us with large amounts of fiber, vitamins and few calories. Using them raw or cooked enriches meals and helps maintain weight. You should take 4 or 5 servings daily, 2 or 3 of fruit, 2 or 3 of vegetables, SKIMMED DAIRY. We must always eat all dairy products skimmed regardless of age. They provide us with all the nutrients but without saturated fat. SMALL PACKAGES. Always using small pots helps control the quantity, and avoids going overboard and having leftovers. ADEQUATE RATIONS. Always cook portions according to the diners. Do not overcook. He will always eat the one who is least convenient for him. NON-STICK POT. They help us cook with less fat, and avoid frying. YES TO THE MICROWAVE- NO TO THE FRYER. Cooking in the microwave is quick and clean and allows you to cook without fat, it is ideal for dieting. The fryer, apart from providing many calories to the diet, overheats the oil a lot and toxic fats can appear. IRON, STEAM, BAKE. They are simple, tasty ways of cooking that do not require fat. Very memorable in weight loss diets LITTLE SALT AND MORE SEASONINGS. Go out as little as possible. If you can use seasonings (herbs, pepper, lemon, etc.)

title: 3. Choosing foods
text: General summary on how to best choose foods within a balanced diet.

title: 4. Foods that you should eat
text:
Cereals: All (bread, pasta, rice, flour), preferably whole grains. They should be taken daily for breakfast and lunch. Legumes: Take two or three times a week, in a stew or salad, in moderate amounts and without fat. Dairy: Always skimmed and in moderate quantities. Proteins: Lean meats, poultry, eggs and fish of all kinds. Fats: Only olive oil, preferably virgin, without going overboard.
3-5 tablespoons a day. Drinks: Water as main liquid; infusions, coffee or tea with sweetener; natural juices; moderate red wine only when appropriate.

title: 5. Foods to avoid
text: Avoid sugars and pastries, chocolates, candies and ice cream. Reduce fats such as butter, cream, bacon, mayonnaise, fried foods and fatty cheeses. Avoid fried foods in general and replace them with iron, steam, oven or microwave. Reduce salt, fatty sausages and alcoholic or sugary drinks as much as possible.

title: 6. Eat healthy
text: Eat varied in small quantities, prioritize homemade food, include fruit and vegetables daily, eat lean proteins, use olive oil without abuse, prefer whole grains, avoid excess sweets and fats, moderate salt and sugary drinks, and maintain hydration with water.

title: 7. Good habits
text: Plan menus, do not store visible caloric foods, have breakfast daily, serve already rationed dishes, eat on a small plate, chew slowly, divide your intake into 4 or 5 meals, avoid snacking between meals and increase daily physical activity.

title: 8. Avoid excess weight
text: Maintain order in meals, do not skip breakfast, avoid snacking between meals, limit foods that encourage binge eating, prioritize fruit/vegetables/whole grains/lean proteins, avoid ultra-processed foods, cook with low-fat techniques and increase daily physical activity.

title: 9. Make a menu
text:
Build a varied and appetizing menu: daily vegetables, daily fruit, better whole grains, low-fat proteins at each meal, legumes
2-3 times a week, fish 3 times a week, olive oil in moderation, low-fat dairy and little salt/sugar.

title: 10. Change foods for others
text: Use ration equivalences between proteins, cereals, fruits and vegetables, dairy products and fats to exchange foods without adjusting amounts or calories in the diet.

title: 11. Control food anxiety
text:
Do not skip meals, eat slowly, do
4-5 meals a day, avoid snacking, use alternatives such as fruit or low-fat dairy products for sweets, remove foods that pose a risk to your eyesight, look for alternative activities for anxiety and ask for professional help if you have binge eating.

title: 12. Calories in drinks
text: Comparison of calories in frequent drinks to choose options with lower energy intake: water, zero/light soft drinks, non-alcoholic beer or infusions versus alcohols, sugary soft drinks and sweet drinks.

title: 13. Eating as a family
text: Eating as a family improves habits, food education and adherence. Maintain a complete breakfast, encourage fruit/vegetables/legumes/fish, limit ultra-processed foods, avoid using food as a reward and reinforce daily physical activity.

title: 14. Prepare light tapas
text: Recipes for light tapas with vegetables, fruits, seafood and low-fat dairy products to snack with calorie control without losing variety or flavor.

title: 15. Home equivalents
text: Home measurements guide: glass, tablespoons, handfuls and portions to estimate grams and milliliters without a scale and better control daily intake.

title: 16. Avoid constipation
text: Do not self-medicate with laxatives, maintain regular schedules, drink at least 2 liters of water, exercise daily, eat fruit with washed skin, vegetables in main meals, whole grains and legumes frequently, and fermented dairy products.

title: 17. Low-calorie alternatives
text: Practical substitutions: change breakfasts, snacks, snacks and high-calorie-dense meals for lighter and more balanced alternatives.

title: 18. Differentiate dairy products
text: How to choose dairy products according to lactose, fat and needs: prioritize skimmed foods, review portions, differentiate vegetable drinks from dairy products and understand the caloric impact of milk, yogurt and cheese.
